title: Receipts/SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.cs: requirement test fails on base (2/4), passes on head (4/4); refutes 2 lens claim(s): requirement-tests-1, requirement-tests-2

refutes.claim: The only code change makes `TypeCollector` tolerate duplicate or mixed keys: `continue` after MsgPack005, and `ContainsKey` guards before `Dictionary.Add`. No visible hunk touches how `SuppressSourceGeneration = true` types are routed through analysis. If the 3.1.1 regression is that suppressed types skip validation entirely, rather than the analyzer throwing on them, then valid-but-wrong suppressed types (for example a public member missing `[Key]`) still get no MsgPack004/003/012. That would leave the core requirement unmet, while the README added in this change claims these diagnostics are reported.

The new `ContainsKey` guards silently drop the second member that shares a key. This prevents the crash, but it is only correct if a duplicate-key diagnostic is reported elsewhere. No hunk shows a diagnostic for duplicate keys, yet the README now states that MsgPack005 enforces unique keys. If none is emitted, a suppressed type with duplicate keys passes analysis silently and then fails or misbehaves at run time in the dynamic resolver.

title: Receipts/DuplicateKeyDiagnosticTests.cs: edge-case test passes on head (2 tests): no defect shown; refutes 1 lens claim(s): logic-edge-1

refutes.claim: Duplicate keys now pass silently. A [MessagePackObject] with two members sharing [Key(0)] (or the same string key) previously made `intMembers.Add` / `stringMembers.Add` throw. That surfaced as AD0001/CS8785, so the problem was visible. The new `ContainsKey` guard keeps the first member and drops the second without reporting anything. With no diagnostic, the analyzer stops flagging a type that the dynamic resolver rejects at run time ('key is duplicated'). For types that are not suppressed, the generated formatter silently omits the second member, so its data is lost on round-trip.
